title: ML evaluation methodology
subtitle: Frozen evaluation sets, pre-registered targets, known-answer controls, a list of results never to quote, and a baseline built to beat me. It tied, and the tie is what I publish.

stats.label: tokens of tool catalog the model replaces
crossed over across two cards to attribute a throughput gain

lede: Capabilities model replaces a whole tool catalog with one discovery tool backed by a fine-tuned 0.6-billion-parameter open-weight base model. A model like that is only worth publishing if its evaluation can catch it being wrong, so I built the evaluation as an instrument with fixed rules before any result came in. Its core is a frozen pair: a held-out query set and a set of long probes in which the needed tool is buried deep inside a verbose request. Nothing about the instrument could move to help the model. Every comparison is like for like, and I keep a written list of results that must not be quoted, with the reason beside each.
quote: Known-answer controls run inside the harness so it can catch the team as readily as the model.
evidence: ML evaluation methodology: a frozen held-out set and 15 buried-request probes fixed before any result, with known-answer controls that stopped the whole matrix when one failed.
Baseline engineering: a dense and BM25 fusion baseline with every constant swept and an embedder chosen from 5 in a bake-off, which tied the fine-tuned model.
Reporting negative results: published 0.67 against 0.90 recall on buried requests and 6.9 against a 200 requests-a-second serving target.
author: Corey James
